cases.title: New learner opening on a busy comp

The opening proposes only Title and names its 4 pairs (Position ×2, Scale, Opacity). The other layers appear only as a count ("11 keyframe pairs... spread over 6 layers").

The opening names hidden_layers Old Take ("hidden, so I'll skip it") and precomp_layers Icon. It does not imply Icon is fine: "I can't see inside precomps yet, so I'm not saying it's fine, only that I haven't checked it."

Every name and time matches the snapshot_project result: Mentor Practice, Title Position 0.5–1.5 s and 1.5–3 s, Scale 0.5–1.5 s, Opacity 0.5–1.5 s, Old Take, and Icon. The count of 6 layers (Title, Subtitle, CTRL, Bar, Glow, Old Take) is also correct.
This is a new learner: read_learner_record returned empty skills and lessons, and the mentor claims no earlier history in the opening.

Turn 2 ends with "Your turn: ease Title's 4 pairs" and lists all four by property and time, no set_ease is called, and the only offer is to show one pair if the learner gets stuck.

rubric.reason: Before the first explanation in Turn 2, the mentor called preview_frame at time 1, inside the focus pair Title › Position 0.5 s → 1.5 s, and the reply refers to it: "pulled up the frame at 1 s, halfway through Title's first Position move."

The only edit is one set_ease on the demo_target (1/ADBE Transform Group/ADBE Position/1), and the reply ends with "Your turn. Ease these 3 pairs on Title yourself," naming Position 1.5 s → 3 s, Scale 0.5 s → 1.5 s and Opacity 0.5 s → 1.5 s.

Turn 2 asks the learner to ease the three remaining Title pairs and names them (Position 1.5 s → 3 s, Scale 0.5 s → 1.5 s, Opacity 0.5 s → 1.5 s), and Turn 3 warmly declines 'do the rest' with a reason ('Easing the rest yourself is what makes it stick') without offering to do it.

cases.title: A returning learner picks up what was still wrong
